Now I'll identify smokers (via Observation "Current smoker" concepts) and count their cancer diagnoses in the last 2 years. I'll use `concept_ancestor` to capture all malignant neoplasm descendants of concept 443392.

arguments.sql_query:
SELECT TOP 20 c.condition_concept_id, con.concept_name, COUNT(DISTINCT c.person_id) AS n_patients, COUNT(*) AS n_diagnoses
FROM omop.condition_occurrence c
JOIN omop.concept con ON con.concept_id = c.condition_concept_id
JOIN omop.concept_ancestor ca ON ca.descendant_concept_id = c.condition_concept_id AND ca.ancestor_concept_id = 443392
WHERE c.condition_start_date >= '2024-07-27' AND c.condition_start_date <= '2026-07-27'
AND c.person_id IN (
    SELECT DISTINCT o.person_id
    FROM omop.observation o
    WHERE o.observation_concept_id IN (2101895, 903664, 40766945)
       OR o.value_as_concept_id IN (45881517, 45884037, 45878118, 45884038, 36309332, 36307857, 36307682, 45881686, 45883387, 45881518)
)
GROUP BY c.condition_concept_id, con.concept_name
ORDER BY n_patients DESC

## Most frequent cancer diagnoses in smokers (last 2 years)

Cohort: patients with a coded current-smoker status (n=144) and a malignant-neoplasm diagnosis dated 2024-07-27 to 2026-07-27, ranked by number of distinct patients.

| Cancer diagnosis | Patients | Diagnosis records |
|---|---|---|
| Primary malignant neoplasm of prostate | 5 | 60 |
| Malignant neoplasm of prostate | 4 | 18 |
| Primary malignant neoplasm of respiratory tract | 2 | 22 |
| Malignant neoplasm of upper lobe of left lung | 2 | 26 |
| Malignant neoplasm of upper lobe of lung | 2 | 77 |
| Carcinoma of prostate | 2 | 13 |
| Malignant neoplasm of skin | 2 | 2 |
| Primary malignant neoplasm of breast | 2 | 58 |

Grouped by cancer type, the leaders are **prostate cancer**, **lung/respiratory cancer**, and **breast cancer**.

Important caveats:
- **Small denominator.** Only 144 patients in the whole database have a structured current-smoker observation, so patient counts per diagnosis are tiny (max 5). Smoking status is largely under-coded here; a more complete cohort would need note/NLP or drug-based inference.
- **Definition of "smoker"** = current-smoker concepts in the `observation` table (SNOMED/LOINC/CPT4 status codes); former smokers are excluded.
- **"Last 2 years"** anchored to today (2024-07-27 → 2026-07-27); raw `condition_start_date` values range implausibly (to 2203), so date filtering matters.
- Diagnoses use SNOMED descendants of "Malignant neoplastic disease" (443392) and are counted at the granular concept level, so the same cancer appears under several near-synonym codes (e.g., three prostate variants).

Want me to collapse near-synonym codes into higher-level cancer categories, or broaden the smoker definition to include former/heavy smokers?
